proposed.name: S_eta
proposed.def: For every ambient tuple \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(S_g\) is its finite set of selection vertices, disjoint from \(V\). The notation \(S\) without a subscript remains the generic selection-set variable used in member assumptions.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Selection vertices are a component of each compatible model and must be allowed to change under graphical replacement.

proposed_core_edits.name: S_star

proposed.name: S_star
proposed.def: For \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(S_g^*\in\{0,1\}^{|S_g|}\) is the counterfactual basal-world selection-status vector; a unit from model \(g\) is observed exactly on \(S_g^*=\mathbf 1\). When \(\eta\) is fixed, \(S^*\) abbreviates \(S_\eta^*\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The basal selection-status vector must be indexed by the model-specific selection set.

proposed_core_edits.name: G0

proposed.name: G0
proposed.def: For a model tuple \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(G_0(g)\) is its basal selected DAG on the disjoint vertex union \(V\dot\cup S_g\).
proposed.role: common basal structure within a model tuple

proposed_core_edits.reason: The domain of the basal DAG must use the selection vertices belonging to its own tuple.

proposed.name: kappa
proposed.def: For \(g\in\mathcal G_{D,K}\), \(\kappa_v^{(j)}(g)(dx_v\mid x_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(g)}(v)})\) is the regime-\(j\) local conditional kernel at \(v\in V\dot\cup S_g\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Kernel indexing must follow the model-specific vertex domain.

proposed.def: \(\eta=(S_\eta,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},(\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K})\) is a fully specified selected-intervention model tuple; its law-level members also carry the coupled exogenous variables and response functions required by the model-class definition.

proposed.name: A
proposed.def: For each model \(\eta\), \(A(\eta)=\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta)}(\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(\eta)}(S_\eta))\cap V\), including the observed parents of every selection vertex belonging to \(\eta\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Selection ancestry must be computed from the selection set of the same model.

proposed.def: \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), defined in \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\), is the note's positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass of the graphical selected-intervention models of Dai et al.
proposed.role: law-level faithful subclass used by the endpoint-invariance target

proposed.name: RepGraph
proposed.type: selection-set, graph, and target specification map
proposed.def: \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\) is the purely graphical replacement specification constructed in \(\mathrm{def:basal\mbox{-}replacement}\); it contains a selection-node set, a basal selected DAG on \(V\dot\cup\widetilde S\), and direct-target sets, but no probability kernels.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement output must include the enlarged selection set explicitly.

proposed_core_edits.name: Real

proposed.name: Real
proposed.def: If \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)=(\widetilde S,\widetilde G_0,(\widetilde T_k)_{k=1}^{K})\), then \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\) contains exactly the law-level models \(\widetilde\eta\) in \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) with \(S_{\widetilde\eta}=\widetilde S\), \(G_0(\widetilde\eta)=\widetilde G_0\), and \(T_k(\widetilde\eta)=\widetilde T_k\) for every \(k\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Realization must enforce equality of selection vertices as well as graph and targets.

proposed.condition:
For every \(\eta\), there exist exogenous variables \((U_v)_{v\in V\cup S_\eta}\) with a single product law shared by all regimes, measurable observed-variable response functions \(f_v^{(j)}\), \(v\in V\), \(j=0,\ldots,K\), and basal selection responses \(f_s^*\), \(s\in S_\eta\), such that
\[
 X_v^{(j)}=f_v^{(j)}\!\left(X_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(\eta)}(v)\cap V}^{(j)},U_v\right),
 \qquad v\in V,
 \qquad j=0,\ldots,K,
\]
and the selection event is generated once in the basal world by
\[
 S_{\eta,s}^*=f_s^*\!\left(X_{\operatorname{pa}_{G_0(\eta)}(s)}^{(0)},U_s\right),
 \qquad s\in S_\eta.
\]
The induced observed-variable local conditional kernels are \(\kappa_v^{(j)}(\eta)\), the selection kernels satisfy \(\kappa_s^{(j)}(\eta)=\kappa_s^{(0)}(\eta)\), and
\[
 f_v^{(k)}=f_v^{(0)}\quad(v\in V\setminus T_k(\eta)),
 \qquad k\in[K].
\]
For every \(j=0,\ldots,K\), the selected arm law is
\[
 P_\eta^{(j)}=\mathcal L_\eta\!\left((X_v^{(j)})_{v\in V}\mid S_\eta^*=\mathbf1\right).
\]
Thus all arms are obtained from one coupled response-function family by conditioning on the same pre-intervention basal event.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The regimewise factorization assumption must require that all regime laws arise from one coupled Dai twin SCM rather than from unrelated factorizations.

proposed.name: Finite-alphabet faithful shared-response subclass of Dai graphical models
proposed.construction:
Let \(S_\eta\) denote the selection-vertex component of \(\eta\), and instantiate every occurrence of the generic selection set \(S\) in the member assumptions below by \(S_\eta\). Define
\[
\begin{split}
\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}
:=\bigl\{\eta={}&\bigl(S_\eta,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},
                    (\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K}\bigr)
                    \in\mathcal G_{D,K}:\\
&D\in\mathbb N_+,\ K\in\mathbb N_0,\ \eta\text{ satisfies }
\mathrm{ass:basal\mbox{-}dag},
\mathrm{ass:causal\mbox{-}sufficiency},
\mathrm{ass:selection\mbox{-}structure},
\mathrm{ass:selection\mbox{-}parent\mbox{-}domain},\\
&\mathrm{ass:markov\mbox{-}factorization},
\mathrm{ass:selection\mbox{-}event\mbox{-}positivity},
\mathrm{ass:pretreatment\mbox{-}selection},
\mathrm{ass:soft\mbox{-}intervention},
\mathrm{ass:twin\mbox{-}faithfulness}
\bigr\}.
\end{split}
\]
Thus \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) is the note's finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass of the graphical selected-intervention models of Dai et al.; the notation does not assert equality with every law-level model allowed by that paper.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The model class must index selection sets by the model, require one shared-response twin SCM, and be described as a faithful finite-alphabet subclass rather than the entire published law class.

proposed.name: Selected-subgraph graphical replacement
proposed.construction:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), put \(A=A(\eta)\), and let \(B\) be an admissible directed graph on \(A\). For each \(x\in A\) and each \(xy\in E(H[A])\), choose mutually distinct fresh selection labels \(s_x\) and \(s_{xy}=s_{yx}\), none belonging to \(S_\eta\), and define
\[
 \widetilde S
 :=S_\eta\,\dot\cup\,\{s_x:x\in A\}
       \,\dot\cup\,\{s_{xy}:xy\in E(H[A])\}.
\]
Define the basal DAG \(\widetilde G_0\) on \(V\dot\cup\widetilde S\) by
\[
\begin{split}
 E(\widetilde G_0):={}&
 \bigl(E(G_0(\eta))\setminus E(G_0(\eta)[A])\bigr)
 \cup E(B)\\
 &\cup\{x\to s_x:x\in A\}
 \cup\{x\to s_{xy},\ y\to s_{xy}:xy\in E(H[A])\}.
\end{split}
\]
For each \(k\in[K]\), retain every exterior direct target in \(T_k(\eta)\setminus A\). Inside \(A\), let \(\widetilde T_k\cap A\) consist exactly of those \(v\in Z_k\cap A\) that are not proper descendants in \(\widetilde G_0\) of another vertex of \(Z_k\cap A\) or of a retained target in \(T_k(\eta)\setminus A\). Set
\[
 \widetilde T_k
 :=\bigl(T_k(\eta)\setminus A\bigr)\cup(\widetilde T_k\cap A),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)
 :=\bigl(\widetilde S,\widetilde G_0,(\widetilde T_k)_{k=1}^{K}\bigr).
\]
This is a purely graphical selection-set, DAG, and target specification. It supplies neither probability kernels nor a law-level replacement model.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Fresh childless selection vertices must be part of an explicit replacement selection set and of the vertex domain of the replacement DAG.

proposed.name: Fully specified shared-response replacement realization fiber
proposed.construction:
If
\[
 \operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)
 =\bigl(\widetilde S,\widetilde G_0,(\widetilde T_k)_{k=1}^{K}\bigr),
\]
define
\[
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)
 :=\left\{\widetilde\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}:
 S_{\widetilde\eta}=\widetilde S,\quad
 G_0(\widetilde\eta)=\widetilde G_0,\quad
 T_k(\widetilde\eta)=\widetilde T_k\ \text{for every }k\in[K]
 \right\}.
\]
Membership therefore requires equality of the selection-set, basal-DAG, and direct-target components. The kernel family \(\kappa(\widetilde\eta)\), the shared exogenous law, and the response functions belong to each member \(\widetilde\eta\); none is inherited from \(\eta\). In particular, the fresh childless selection vertices introduced by \(\operatorname{RepGraph}\) must be realized inside the declared ambient tuple and model class.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The realization predicate must require exact equality of the enlarged selection set so that fresh selection vertices belong to the realized ambient tuple.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) is the endpoint-invariance structural target over the note's finite-alphabet faithful shared-response compatibility fiber. On the separate fixed-\(A\) purely graphical fiber, the established result is \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e)=\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)\). At law level, \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{faith}}(e)\subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e)\); singleton \(\mathcal G_A\) gives equality automatically, whereas two-mark equality requires nonempty faithful realization fibers. Equality of a fixed observable rule closure with \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\) remains a conditional implication requiring faithful realization and an unknown-\(A\) extension theorem.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The estimand line must distinguish the exact structural graphical result from the faithful law-level bracket and from the still-conditional unknown-selection conclusion.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: For \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m\) if and only if \(\mu_\eta(e)=m\) for every \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}\) otherwise, where \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) is formed inside the finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\) defined in this note, not the entire published graphical class.
proposed_core_edits.reason: After the class correction, the functional must say explicitly which compatibility fiber supplies endpoint invariance.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 proves CDIS soundness, while p. 8, lines 652--661, states that completeness is uncertain.
proposed.matched_by: This note gives an exact fixed-selection-ancestry theorem on a purely graphical Dai fiber and only a law-level faithful bracket plus conditional endpoint-equality implication; it does not close Dai et al.'s completeness gap or claim the full published law class.

proposed.comparator_claim: Sections 3--4 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for one observational PAG, with Theorem 2 giving a representative-MAG construction.
proposed.matched_by: Zhang's single-MAG construction informs the proposed rule grammar, but no finite common-basal unknown-target multi-regime extension theorem is proved here.

proposed.comparator_claim: Markov equivalence of maximal ancestral graphs is characterized by adjacencies and colliders with order.
proposed.matched_by: Those invariants motivate preservation of each full regime signature; the new exact equality is confined to a structural fixed-\(A\) fiber and does not itself yield faithful law-level witnesses.

proposed.comparator_claim: The public abstract describes a known-target enumeration-based completion; official theorem text was inaccessible.
proposed.matched_by: This note excludes global enumeration as its headline method and leaves the finite observable unknown-target, selected common-basal rule list open.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper gives a complete characterization under soft interventions with unknown targets and no selection bias.
proposed.matched_by: Pre-treatment selection and one shared basal selected DAG add unresolved faithful-realization and unknown-selection extension requirements, so the present result is below that completeness guarantee.

proposed.comparator_claim: The public record describes a sound and complete F-FCI algorithm for latent confounding with post-treatment selection.
proposed.matched_by: The selection timing and model class differ, and this note claims neither a competing complete algorithm nor simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Comparator positioning must reflect the exact graphical theorem, the conditional faithful promotion, and the corrected update count without claiming completeness.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For every admissible replacement specification, first construct a nonempty open rational parameterization of one equality-constrained shared-exogenous shared-response twin-SCM family satisfying the Markov direction; then, for every query that is \(m\)-connected in a replacement MAG, exhibit a parameter point at which at least one cleared conditional-independence determinant is nonzero.
open_obligations.obstruction: Generic faithfulness for unrestricted multinomial DAGs does not imply polynomial nontriviality after non-target response equalities, a common basal selection event, shared exogenous variables, and fixed one-half pooled weights are imposed. The frozen core supplies neither the required parameter-space construction nor a cross-world coupling that witnesses each atomic dependence.
open_obligations.attempted: Used the established exceptional-set reduction to isolate all unfaithfulness events as finitely many determinant zero sets and the product-polynomial argument to obtain one simultaneous point once atomic nontriviality holds. This route cannot prove that the equality-constrained parameter space is nonempty and open for every replacement or that no required determinant vanishes identically on it.
open_obligations.partial_result: For any supplied nonempty open set \(\Theta\subset\mathbb R^r\) that rationally parameterizes equality-constrained shared-response-function models, has strictly positive cells and denominators, and satisfies the Markov direction, conditional independence is equivalent to finitely many cleared determinant-polynomial equations. For each \(m\)-connected query choose one determinant polynomial \(q_i\) that is not identically zero. Because \(\Theta\) is nonempty and open and \(\prod_i q_i\) is a nonzero polynomial, some \(\theta^\star\in\Theta\) satisfies \(\prod_i q_i(\theta^\star)\ne0\). At this common point all pooled selected laws are simultaneously faithful. Conversely, any simultaneously faithful point makes at least one determinant for each \(m\)-connected query nonzero and hence certifies its nontriviality. Positive local tables provide factorization, non-target response stability, and positive selection. What remains unproved is both the construction of a suitable nonempty open rational shared-response parameterization for every replacement specification and the atomic nontriviality certificate on that constrained parameter space.

prose_updates.tldr: Selection before perturbation couples all pooled regime MAGs through one basal selected DAG. The note now proves the exact fixed-\(A\) endpoint mark set on a purely graphical Dai fiber and separates it from the law-level faithful bracket: singleton graphical mark sets identify the faithful endpoint automatically, while opposing faithful witnesses in the two-mark case still require nonempty realization fibers. A supplied nonempty open rational shared-response parameterization yields a finite exceptional-set argument only after atomic determinant nontriviality is certified. The parameterization construction, those atomic certificates, the finite observable unknown-\(A\) rule list, canonical endpoint equality, and simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs remain open.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. prove CDIS soundness and leave completeness uncertain; their graphical endpoint semantics do not supply opposing faithful representatives from one shared-response twin SCM. Zhang proves completeness for one observational PAG, not synchronized pooled intervention MAGs with unknown targets and pre-treatment selection. The exact remaining law-level gap is twofold: construct a nonempty open equality-constrained shared-response parameterization for every replacement specification and prove atomic determinant nontriviality on it. Even an affirmative realization theorem would still leave the finite observable unknown-\(A\) common-exterior extension problem.
project_justification.niche: The achieved contribution is an exact structural characterization on the fixed-\(A\) purely graphical fiber, together with a sharply separated faithful-model bracket and conditional endpoint-equality theorem. It is a technical foundation below a complete-calculus result, not a field-level completeness or inference theorem.
project_justification.fill: The note exposes three distinct maps. It computes \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\) by explicit empty-graph and simple signature-monotone-path constructions; it embeds the nonempty faithful mark set inside that graphical set, obtaining automatic equality only in singleton cases; and it proves that faithful realization plus a fixed observable unknown-\(A\) extension property would imply equality of a candidate rule closure with the canonical SI-PAG. Conditional saturation needs at most \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates. Neither open antecedent is silently inferred from graphical inclusion.

sampling_model.design: Oracle graphical analysis uses the observational selected-law MAG signature and \(K\) pooled binary-indicator MAG signatures coupled by one model-specific basal selected DAG. The structural target is endpoint invariance over the note's finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass; the established results are exact on a separate fixed-\(A\) graphical fiber and conditional at the unknown-\(A\) law level.
sampling_model.units: The primitive law-level object is \(\eta=(S_\eta,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K},(\kappa^{(j)}(\eta))_{j=0}^{K})\), generated by one shared-exogenous response-function family. At \(K=0\), its oracle law is \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S_\eta^*=\mathbf1)\); for each \(k\in[K]\), the comparison uses the pooled law \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Regime membership is observed. Each direct soft-intervention target set \(T_k(\eta)\) is latent and may differ from the indicator-neighbor set \(Z_k\), which can also contain indirectly affected ancestrally selected variables.
sampling_model.overlap: The common basal selection event \(S_\eta^*=\mathbf1\) has positive probability for every law-level model, so all selected and pooled oracle laws are defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not applicable to the proved oracle statements. No finite-sample conditional-independence or invariance tests, separation margin, or simultaneous error-control theorem is assumed or established.

prose_updates.related_work: Dai et al.'s Lemmas 3--6 provide the graphical twin-MAG interface for causally sufficient, childless pre-treatment selection, while their Theorem 3 establishes CDIS soundness and their discussion leaves completeness uncertain. The present note uses a finite-alphabet, positive-selection, pooled-law-faithful shared-response subclass of those graphical models and does not claim equality with Dai et al.'s full law class. Zhang's Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2 establish arrowhead and tail completeness for a single observational PAG, but not simultaneous common-basal pooled regimes. Ali, Richardson, and Spirtes provide single-MAG equivalence invariants that motivate full-signature preservation, not faithful common-basal realization. The public Zhou--Kocaoglu abstract concerns known-target completion with enumeration, which is excluded here as a headline calculus. Wang, Du, and Zhou inform computational context; the present computable statement is only the conditional bound of \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict endpoint updates for a supplied fixed rule list. Jaber et al. treat unknown targets without selection, and Luo et al. concern a distinct post-treatment-selection setting. Relative to these comparators, the result is an exact fixed-\(A\) graphical theorem and a conditional law-level implication, not completeness.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: A graphical replacement now specifies \(\widetilde S\), \(\widetilde G_0\), and \(\widetilde T\) explicitly, but this does not construct a law-level model. The exceptional-set argument is conditional on first supplying a nonempty open rational parameterization of equality-constrained shared-exogenous response-function models that satisfies the Markov direction, strict positivity, and positive denominators. Constructing that parameterization for every replacement and showing one determinant is nonzero for every \(m\)-connected query are both open. Moreover, exact equality on the fixed-\(A\) graphical fiber does not infer faithful two-mark witnesses, and neither result supplies a finite observable unknown-\(A\) rule list or a common exterior completion. No separation margin or finite-sample test theorem is present, so simultaneous confidence SI-PAGs are outside the proved scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Proved content is an exact fixed-selection-ancestry endpoint characterization on a purely structural Dai graphical fiber, \(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\mathcal G_A\), obtained by necessity and explicit empty-graph or simple signature-monotone-path constructions. At law level the proved relation is \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{faith}}\subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}\), with equality automatic for singleton \(\mathcal G_A\) and conditional on nonempty realization fibers for two marks. The finite polynomial exceptional-set argument is valid only for a supplied nonempty open rational shared-response parameterization satisfying the Markov direction and atomic nontriviality. The construction of that parameterization, the atomic certificates, opposing faithful two-mark witnesses, a fixed observable unknown-\(A\) extension calculus, unconditional canonical SI-PAG equality, and simultaneous finite-sample confidence guarantees remain open. If a fixed polynomial-time rule list satisfying the two open antecedents is later supplied, its closure has at most \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates and equals the canonical target by a conditional implication. The scope excludes latent common causes among measured variables, post-treatment or regime-specific selection, and a global basal-DAG enumerator as the headline method.

statement_notes.justification: This open question isolates faithful promotion from the exact graphical theorem; the established algebraic result applies only after a suitable rational shared-response parameterization and atomic determinant certificates are supplied.
statement_notes.gap: Both the nonempty open equality-constrained parameterization for an arbitrary replacement and determinant nontriviality for each \(m\)-connected query remain open.
statement_notes.consumer: An affirmative result would promote the two graphical endpoint constructions to faithful law-level witnesses, but would not by itself solve unknown-\(A\) completeness.

proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(g=\operatorname{gr}(\eta)\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:exact\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}a\mbox{-}graphical\mbox{-}frontier}\),
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g)
 =\mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\tag{1}
\]
Discarding the middle term proves the required nonempty inclusion.  In either singleton case in the definition of \(\mathcal G_A\), a nonempty subset of that singleton equals it, so (1) gives the two asserted law-level identifications.

If \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\), the same lemma proves that \(B_0\) and every simple-path graph \(B_P\) are admissible; their replacement specifications preserve \(A(\eta)\) and the complete graphical signature on every \(U_j\), and their marks at \(e\) are respectively \(\mathtt{arrow}\) and \(\mathtt{tail}\).  If both displayed realization fibers are nonempty, \(\mathrm{lem:replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\) promotes one member of each fiber, not the bare graphical specifications themselves, into \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\).  The two opposite marks then belong to \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)\); (1) and the two-element definition of \(\mathcal G_A\) give the asserted equality.  The interpretation of \(Z_k\) follows from the indicator-neighbor identity, and the exclusion of retained adjacencies is certified by \(\mathrm{prop:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}reduction}\). \(\square\)

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(k\in[K]\), and an intervention-created observed adjacency \(uv\), where \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), \(uv\notin H\), and \(uv\) is present in the regime-\(k\) skeleton.  Let \(e=(k,u\mid uv)\) and put \(g=\operatorname{gr}(\eta)\).  Then
\[
 \varnothing\ne
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq
 \mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g)
 =\mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\]
Consequently, if \(u\notin Z_k\), both the law-level and graphical mark sets equal \(\{\mathtt{tail}\}\), while if \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=0\), both equal \(\{\mathtt{arrow}\}\).  If \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\), the specifications \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_0)\) and \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_P)\), where \(B_0\) is empty and \(B_P\) is the directed-edge graph of any simple \(u\)-to-\(v\) path in \(L_{A(\eta)}\), belong to \(\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g)\) and attain respectively \(\mathtt{arrow}\) and \(\mathtt{tail}\) at \(e\).  Hence the graphical equality is unconditional.  In this two-mark case, the further law-level equality
\[
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 =\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g)
 =\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}
\]
follows if \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0)\ne\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P)\ne\varnothing\).  No graphical member is promoted to a faithful law-level member merely from its membership in \(\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}\), and no target-membership equivalence is asserted for retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(A=A(\eta)\) and \(g=\operatorname{gr}(\eta)\).  We first establish the graphical outer bound.  Take any
\(widetilde g\in\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g)\) and set
\(\widetilde A=A_{\mathrm{gr}}(\widetilde g)=A\) and
\(\widetilde F_\ell=\operatorname{de}_{G_{\widetilde g}}(T_{\widetilde g,\ell})\cap V\).
Because \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{gr}}(\widetilde g)=\mathcal O\), the indicator-neighbor set in its regime-\(\ell\) twin projection is the observed set \(Z_\ell\).  The indicator-neighbor identity in \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\), which is a statement about the Dai twin graph and its latent projection, gives
\[
 Z_\ell
 =T_{\widetilde g,\ell}
  \cup\bigl((\widetilde F_\ell\setminus T_{\widetilde g,\ell})
            \cap\widetilde A\bigr).
\tag{1}
\]
Since \(T_{\widetilde g,\ell}\subseteq\widetilde F_\ell\) and \(x\in\widetilde A\), (1) yields, for every \(x\in A\),
\[
 x\in Z_\ell\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\widetilde F_\ell.
\tag{2}
\]

The adjacency \(uv\) is absent from the observational skeleton and present in regime \(k\), so it is not a retained observational edge.  The exhaustive non-retained endpoint cases in \(\mathrm{lem:dai\mbox{-}twin\mbox{-}mag\mbox{-}interface}\), together with (2), imply
\[
 \mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\widetilde g}(e)=\mathtt{arrow}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u\in Z_k,
\tag{3}
\]
and
\[
 \mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\widetilde g}(e)=\mathtt{tail}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 u\notin Z_k\ \text{ or }\
 u\in\operatorname{An}_{G_{\widetilde g}}(v).
\tag{4}
\]
Suppose the second alternative in (4) holds.  Since \(u\ne v\), choose a nonempty directed path
\[
 u=x_0\to x_1\to\cdots\to x_r=v
\tag{5}
\]
in \(G_{\widetilde g}\).  A selection vertex cannot occur on (5), because all selection vertices are childless.  Moreover, \(v\in\widetilde A\) is an ancestor of a parent of a selection vertex, so every ancestor \(x_i\) of \(v\) has the same property.  Thus every \(x_i\) belongs to \(\widetilde A=A\).  By the basal-edge clause of the same twin-MAG interface, every edge \(x_ix_{i+1}\) is an observational adjacency and hence lies in \(H[A]\).

Fix \(\ell\in[K]\).  If \(\ell\in\sigma(x_i)\), then \(x_i\in Z_\ell\), so (2) gives \(x_i\in\widetilde F_\ell\).  Descendant closure of \(\widetilde F_\ell\) along \(x_i\to x_{i+1}\), followed by (2), gives \(x_{i+1}\in Z_\ell\).  Hence
\[
 \sigma(x_i)\subseteq\sigma(x_{i+1}),
 \qquad i=0,\ldots,r-1.
\tag{6}
\]
Equations (5)--(6) exhibit a directed path from \(u\) to \(v\) in \(L_A\); therefore
\[
 u\in\operatorname{An}_{G_{\widetilde g}}(v)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Reach}_{A}(u,v)=1.
\tag{7}
\]
Combining (3), (4), and (7), and then using the three-case definition of \(\mathcal G_A\), proves
\[
 \mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g)
 \subseteq\mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\tag{8}
\]

The graphical reduct \(g=\operatorname{gr}(\eta)\) belongs to
\(\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g)\), because
\(A_{\mathrm{gr}}(g)=A(\eta)\) and
\(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{gr}}(g)=\mathcal O(\eta)=\mathcal O\).  Thus the left-hand side of (8) is nonempty.  If \(u\notin Z_k\), (8) and the definition of \(\mathcal G_A\) give
\(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\{\mathtt{tail}\}\).  If
\(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A}(u,v)=0\), they give
\(\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}=\{\mathtt{arrow}\}\).  These are the two singleton cases.

It remains to prove the reverse inclusion in the two-mark case.  Assume
\(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A}(u,v)=1\).  Let \(B_0\) be the graph on \(A\) with no edges.  It is acyclic, is a subgraph of \(H[A]\), satisfies signature monotonicity vacuously, and creates no unshielded collider.  Hence it is admissible for
\(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\).  In the replacement graph, there is no directed path from \(u\) to \(v\).  Indeed, there is no edge within \(A\), and no retained edge can enter \(A\) from \(V\setminus A\): such an entering vertex would be an ancestor of a vertex of \(A\), hence an ancestor of a selection parent, and would itself belong to \(A\).  A childless selection vertex cannot return to \(V\).  The replacement-preservation lemma also gives the unchanged indicator-neighbor identity, so (2) applied to the replacement makes \(u\) affected in regime \(k\).  The non-retained endpoint cases therefore put an arrowhead at \(u\).  Thus
\[
 \operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_0)
 \in\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g),
 \qquad
 \mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_0)}(e)
 =\mathtt{arrow}.
\tag{9}
\]
Here the corrected replacement specification includes its newly constructed selection set; (9) is purely graphical and supplies no kernels.

Because \(A\) is finite, reachability supplies a simple path
\[
 P:u=y_0\to y_1\to\cdots\to y_s=v
\tag{10}
\]
in \(L_A\).  Let \(B_P\) consist exactly of the directed edges in (10).  It is acyclic; each edge lies in \(H[A]\) and satisfies
\(\sigma(y_i)\subseteq\sigma(y_{i+1})\); and every vertex has at most one incoming \(B_P\)-edge, so \(B_P\) creates no unshielded collider.  Thus \(B_P\) is admissible.  In its replacement, \(u\) is an ancestor of \(v\).  The preserved indicator-neighbor identity makes \(u\) affected, and descendant closure along (10) makes \(v\) affected.  The endpoint rule therefore orients this non-retained adjacency as \(u\to v\), giving
\[
 \operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_P)
 \in\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g),
 \qquad
 \mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B_P)}(e)
 =\mathtt{tail}.
\tag{11}
\]
The membership assertions in (9) and (11) use
\(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\): both replacements preserve \(A\), and every skeleton and unshielded collider on every full domain \(U_j\), including the indicator-involving instances.  Equations (8)--(11) prove, in all three cases,
\[
 \mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g)
 =\mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\tag{12}
\]

We now compare this structural quantity with the law-level target.  If
\(\eta'\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\), then the graphical reduct
\(\operatorname{gr}(\eta')\) satisfies
\[
 A_{\mathrm{gr}}(\operatorname{gr}(\eta'))=A(\eta')=A(\eta),
 \qquad
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{gr}}(\operatorname{gr}(\eta'))
 =\mathcal O(\eta')=\mathcal O.
\tag{13}
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{gr}(\eta')\in\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g)\), and equality of the law-level and graphical projections for a reduct gives
\(\mu_{\eta'}(e)=\mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\operatorname{gr}(\eta')}(e)\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq\mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g).
\tag{14}
\]
The set on the left is nonempty because
\(\eta\in\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\).  Combining (12)--(14) proves the displayed nonempty chain and automatic equality in the singleton cases.

Finally suppose both realization fibers in the statement are nonempty.  Choose
\[
 \eta_{\mathtt{arrow}}\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0),
 \qquad
 \eta_{\mathtt{tail}}\in\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P).
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), both are fully specified faithful members of \(\mathcal C_A(\mathcal O,\eta)\).  Their graphical components are precisely the specifications in (9) and (11), including the replacement selection sets, so their endpoint marks are respectively \(\mathtt{arrow}\) and \(\mathtt{tail}\).  Therefore both marks occur in the law-level set, and (14) gives law-level equality with (12).  This last step uses nonemptiness of the two realization fibers; graphical membership alone does not imply it.  The restriction \(uv\notin H\) is essential: \(\mathrm{prop:retained\mbox{-}edge\mbox{-}sanity\mbox{-}reduction}\) supplies a retained edge with an arrowhead at a vertex outside \(Z_k\), so the target-membership endpoint equivalences used above cannot be extended to retained adjacencies. \(\square\)

proposed.name: Purely graphical Dai specifications and reducts
proposed.construction:
For \(D\in\mathbb N_{+}\) and \(K\in\mathbb N_{0}\), let \(\mathfrak G_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai,gr}}\) be the class of tuples
\[
 g=(S_g,G_g,(T_{g,k})_{k=1}^{K})
\]
with the following purely graphical properties.  The set \(S_g\) is finite and disjoint from \(V\); \(G_g\) is a finite directed acyclic graph on \(V\mathbin{\dot\cup}S_g\) with no additional latent vertices; every \(s\in S_g\) is childless and satisfies \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_g}(s)\subseteq V\); and each \(T_{g,k}\) is a subset of \(V\).  The same pair \((S_g,G_g)\) is used in every regime, selection is pre-intervention, and \(T_{g,k}\) is interpreted by Dai et al.'s soft-intervention twin-graph construction.  Write
\[
 A_{\mathrm{gr}}(g)
 :=\operatorname{An}_{G_g}\!\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_{G_g}(S_g)\bigr)\cap V,
 \qquad
 F_{g,k}:=\operatorname{de}_{G_g}(T_{g,k})\cap V.
\]
Let \(M^{\mathrm{gr}}_0(g)\) be the observational selected latent-projection MAG on \(U_0=V\), and, for \(k\in[K]\), let \(M^{\mathrm{gr}}_k(g)\) be the latent-projection MAG on \(U_k=V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) of the associated Dai twin graph.  Define
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{gr}}(g)
 :=\bigl(\operatorname{skel}(M^{\mathrm{gr}}_j(g)),
          \operatorname{UC}(M^{\mathrm{gr}}_j(g))\bigr)_{j=0}^{K}.
\]
For every reported endpoint \(e\) present in this signature, \(\mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_g(e)\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\) is its mark in the appropriate graph \(M^{\mathrm{gr}}_j(g)[V]\).  Finally, for a law-level model \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), let
\[
 \operatorname{gr}(\eta)
 :=\bigl(S_\eta,G_0(\eta),(T_k(\eta))_{k=1}^{K}\bigr),
\]
where \(S_\eta\) denotes the selection-set component of \(\eta\).  Thus \(\operatorname{gr}(\eta)\in\mathfrak G_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai,gr}}\), \(A_{\mathrm{gr}}(\operatorname{gr}(\eta))=A(\eta)\), \(M_j^{\mathrm{gr}}(\operatorname{gr}(\eta))=M_j(\eta)\), and \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{gr}}(\operatorname{gr}(\eta))=\mathcal O(\eta)\).  This definition imposes no probability kernels and no faithfulness or realizability requirement on an arbitrary member of \(\mathfrak G_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai,gr}}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This separates graph-theoretic compatibility from the finite-alphabet faithful law subclass and makes selection sets explicit components.

proposed.name: Fixed-selection graphical compatibility fiber and mark set
proposed.construction:
For \(g\in\mathfrak G_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai,gr}}\) and a full signature \(\mathcal O\), define the purely structural fixed-selection fiber
\[
 \mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g)
 :=\left\{\widetilde g\in\mathfrak G_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai,gr}}:
 A_{\mathrm{gr}}(\widetilde g)=A_{\mathrm{gr}}(g),\quad
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{gr}}(\widetilde g)=\mathcal O\right\}.
\]
For a reported observed endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\), define its graphically attained mark set by
\[
 \mathcal M_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(e;\mathcal O,g)
 :=\left\{\mu^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\widetilde g}(e):
 \widetilde g\in\mathcal C_A^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,g)\right\}.
\]
Membership requires the Dai directed-acyclic, causal-sufficiency, childless-selection, observed-selection-parent, common-pre-intervention-selection, and direct-target conditions through \(\mathfrak G_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai,gr}}\), equality of the ancestral selected set, and equality of every skeleton and unshielded collider on each full domain \(U_j\).  It does not assert the existence of kernels that make \(\widetilde g\) faithful.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact endpoint result needs a computable structural attained-mark set that does not presume faithful kernel realization.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(\eta\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\), \(k\in[K]\), and an intervention-created observed adjacency \(uv\), where \(u,v\in A(\eta)\), \(uv\notin H\), and \(uv\) is present in the regime-\(k\) skeleton. Let \(e\) be the endpoint at \(u\) on \(uv\). Then
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)
 \subseteq \mathcal G_A(u,v;k).
\]
Thus, if \(u\notin Z_k\), then \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{tail}\}\); if \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=0\), then \(\mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\{\mathtt{arrow}\}\). If \(u\in Z_k\) and \(\operatorname{Reach}_{A(\eta)}(u,v)=1\), the empty graph \(B_0\) on \(A(\eta)\) and the directed-edge graph \(B_P\) of any simple \(u\)-to-\(v\) path in \(L_{A(\eta)}\) are admissible and give two common-basal graphical replacement specifications preserving \(A(\eta)\) and every regime skeleton and unshielded collider on the full domains \(U_j\). The former has an arrowhead and the latter a tail at \(e\). In this two-mark case,
\[
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_0)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \operatorname{Real}(\eta,B_P)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal M_A(e;\mathcal O,\eta)=\mathcal G_A(u,v;k)
 =\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
\]
Here \(u\in Z_k\) denotes direct targeting or indirect affectedness within \(A(\eta)\), not necessarily \(u\in T_k(\eta)\). Retained adjacencies \(uv\in H\) are outside this intervention-created-edge bracket.
proposed.justification: The law-level bracket and singleton identifications are corollaries of an exact unconditional graph-only frontier, without promoting a structural specification to a faithful law.
proposed.gap: When the graphical frontier has two marks, law-level equality still requires nonemptiness of both corresponding faithful realization fibers.
proposed.consumer: This separates exact fixed-selection graphical ambiguity from the unresolved kernel-realization and unknown-selection lifting problems.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The claim is retained, but its proof basis is sharpened by the exact graph-only frontier; metadata now states explicitly that faithful promotion in the two-mark case remains conditional.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a finite list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\) whose rule schemata are independent of \(D\) and \(K\). Suppose every rule premise and every path predicate is uniformly decidable in time polynomial in \(D\), \(K\), and the encoding length of \(\mathcal O\), and every strict conclusion monotonically replaces at least one reported circle endpoint by a tail or an arrowhead, with no endpoint subsequently changed. Then saturation computes \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) in polynomial time and makes at most
\[
 (K+1)D(D-1)
\]
strict reported-endpoint updates. The observational skeleton and unshielded colliders on \(U_0=V\), and the complete skeletons and unshielded-collider families of the faithful pooled selected-law signatures on \(U_k\), \(k\in[K]\), including all indicator adjacencies and indicator-involving unshielded colliders, remain immutable inputs. If in addition \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\), the polynomial-time output is the canonical SI-PAG and the procedure does not enumerate \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(L\) be the encoding length of the immutable oracle input \(\mathcal O\). In one regime there are at most \(\binom D2\) observed--observed adjacencies, and each such adjacency has two reported endpoint positions. There are \(K+1\) regimes. Therefore the number \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) of reported endpoint positions obeys
\[
 N_{\mathrm{end}}
 \le (K+1)\,2\binom D2
 =(K+1)D(D-1).
\tag{1}
\]
This count includes no endpoint at an intervention indicator: by the endpoint-domain convention, regime \(0\) reports endpoints on \(U_0=V\), while every regime \(k\in[K]\) reports only observed--observed endpoints from \(U_k=V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).

By the hypothesis on rule conclusions, every strict endpoint update replaces one circle by one element of \(\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\), and monotonicity prevents a second strict update at that endpoint. Charging each strict endpoint update to its unique changed position and using (1) gives
\[
 N_{\mathrm{upd}}
 \le N_{\mathrm{end}}
 \le (K+1)D(D-1).
\tag{2}
\]

It remains to bound the work used to find these updates. Because \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\) is fixed and finite and each schema has finitely many typed vertex and regime placeholders, there are constants \(c,q,r\in\mathbb N_0\), depending only on the rule list, such that one exhaustive scan has at most
\[
 cD^q(K+1)^r
\tag{3}
\]
instantiated rule premises. The uniform premise-decider hypothesis and finiteness of the list provide a polynomial \(p\) for which each instantiated premise, including each path predicate occurring in it, is decided in at most \(p(D,K,L)\) operations. Hence one exhaustive scan costs at most
\[
 cD^q(K+1)^r p(D,K,L).
\tag{4}
\]

Use the deterministic procedure that scans instances in a fixed order, applies the first instance having a strict conclusion, restarts the scan, and stops after a scan with no strict conclusion. Every nonterminal scan causes at least one strict endpoint update, so (2) bounds the number of scans, including the final scan, by \((K+1)D(D-1)+1\). Combining this fact with (4) gives the polynomial bound
\[
 \bigl((K+1)D(D-1)+1\bigr)cD^q(K+1)^r p(D,K,L).
\tag{5}
\]

The initialization is the one in the definition of \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}\). Rule conclusions refine only reported observed endpoints, so the skeleton and unshielded-collider predicates supplied by the complete signatures on every \(U_k\), including predicates involving \(\zeta_k\), are never modified. At termination the state is closed under every rule instance. To see that it is the least closed extension, let \(Q\) be any closed state extending the same initialization. Induct on the performed strict rule applications. The initialization is contained in \(Q\). If the current state is contained in \(Q\), monotonicity of the selected rule carries its satisfied premise to \(Q\), and closedness of \(Q\) supplies the rule's conclusion. Thus the updated state is also contained in \(Q\). The terminal state is consequently contained in every closed extension, and so equals \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) by the definition of the least monotone closure.

Finally, under the additional equality \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)\), substitution identifies the computed closure with the canonical endpoint-invariance SI-PAG. The described procedure reads only \(\mathcal O\), the current endpoint marks, and the rule predicates; it never queries or enumerates \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\). This proves the proposition.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\) be a finite candidate rule list whose schemata are independent of \(D\) and \(K\), and fix a compatible full signature \(\mathcal O\). Assume the following three conditions. First, for every \(\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and every graph \(B\) admissible for the graphical replacement lemma, \(\operatorname{Real}(\xi,B)\ne\varnothing\). Second, the closure is sound: if \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)\) has a definite mark \(m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\) at a reported endpoint \(e\), then \(\mu_\xi(e)=m\) for every \(\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\). Third, for every endpoint \(e\) left circular by the closure and every \(m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}\), there are \(\xi_{e,m}\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\) and a graph \(B_{e,m}\) admissible for the graphical replacement lemma such that every \(\widetilde\xi\in\operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,m},B_{e,m})\) satisfies \(\mu_{\widetilde\xi}(e)=m\). The rule premises use neither latent \(A(\xi)\), a compatible-model or realizability query, nor a global model enumerator. Then
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)
\]
on all reported observed endpoints. If, additionally, every rule premise and path predicate is uniformly decidable in time polynomial in \(D\), \(K\), and the encoding length of \(\mathcal O\), then saturation is polynomial and makes at most \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates. This is a conditional completeness reduction: it asserts neither nonempty faithful realization for the replacement graphs nor the existence of a finite rule list satisfying the observable unknown-\(A\) extension conditions.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary reported endpoint \(e\in\mathcal E(\mathcal O)\). The closure assigns either a definite mark or a circle at \(e\).

Suppose first that
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)(e)
 =m\in\{\mathtt{tail},\mathtt{arrow}\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The soundness hypothesis applied to (1) yields
\[
 \mu_\xi(e)=m
 \qquad\text{for every }\xi\in\mathcal C(\mathcal O).
\tag{2}
\]
By the definition of the canonical endpoint-invariance SI-PAG, (2) is precisely the condition implying
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=m.
\tag{3}
\]

Suppose instead that
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}.
\tag{4}
\]
Apply the opposing-construction hypothesis to (4), once with \(m=\mathtt{tail}\) and once with \(m=\mathtt{arrow}\). It supplies compatible bases \(\xi_{e,\mathtt{tail}},\xi_{e,\mathtt{arrow}}\) and admissible graphs \(B_{e,\mathtt{tail}},B_{e,\mathtt{arrow}}\). The nonempty-realization hypothesis gives
\[
 \operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,\mathtt{tail}},B_{e,\mathtt{tail}})\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Real}(\xi_{e,\mathtt{arrow}},B_{e,\mathtt{arrow}})\ne\varnothing.
\tag{5}
\]
Choose respective members \(\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{tail}}\) and \(\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{arrow}}\) from the two sets in (5). The replacement-preservation lemma implies
\[
 \widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{tail}},\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{arrow}}
 \in\mathcal C(\mathcal O).
\tag{6}
\]
The opposing-construction hypothesis, which applies to every member of each realization set, also gives
\[
 \mu_{\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{tail}}}(e)=\mathtt{tail},
 \qquad
 \mu_{\widetilde\xi_{\mathtt{arrow}}}(e)=\mathtt{arrow}.
\tag{7}
\]
Thus the endpoint mark at \(e\) is not invariant on \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O)\). The circle clause in the definition of the canonical SI-PAG and (7) imply
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O)(e)=\mathtt{circle}.
\tag{8}
\]

Equations (3) and (8) show equality of the two endpoint marks for the arbitrary \(e\). Both partial graphs have the same reported endpoint domain and the same skeleton fixed by \(\mathcal O\); hence endpointwise equality proves
\[
 \operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O)
 =\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O).
\tag{9}
\]

Under the additional uniform polynomial-time premise-decider condition, the exact conditional polynomial-saturation proposition applies to the fixed finite list \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\). It yields polynomial running time and at most \((K+1)D(D-1)\) strict reported-endpoint updates. The proof of (9) used nonempty faithful realization and the observable unknown-\(A\) extension properties only as explicit hypotheses; it did not establish either hypothesis or construct the rule list. This proves the theorem.
